messages:
Maya: Heads-up — ACMEplus asked for per-tenant routing + per-tenant SLO controls as a must-have for their Dedicated bid. They want route-to-model, per-tenant latency floors, and fallback policies. Can we scope this for the next quarter?
Liam: What exactly are they asking for on SLOs? hard latency numbers or percentile SLAs?
Maya: 95th p50 style. Example: 95th <= 120ms for small sync requests; different bucket for long-context. Also tenant-level fallback to cheaper model when capacity constrains.
Sophia: This is basically combining tenant routing (policy engine) + per-tenant SLO enforcement + fallback pipeline. Big infra lift if we want enforcement (throttles, queueing) vs permissive alerts.
Derek: We can do a permissive MVP: expose routing + alerting + recommended fallback rules. Enforcement (hard throttles) would need infra changes and an on-path decision hook.
Maya: Customer expressed "must have" for purchase. Sales says they may walk without enforcement.
Liam: Technical tradeoffs: enforcement needs token accounting per-tenant + admission control. Also affects batching and cost calculations.
Sophia: Ops concerns: per-tenant SLOs means we need per-tenant traces/latency histograms and a dashboard. That we can wire to Console quicker.
Derek: Approx effort estimates — Routing policy + UI: 3w. Per-tenant metrics + dashboard: 2w. Fallback plumbing (model variants + cheap fallback path): 3w. Admission control/enforcement: 4-6w.
Maya: Proposed scope for Q: MVP = routing + dashboards + built-in fallback recommendations (no hard enforcement). Launch criteria: doced config, demo with ACMEplus, 95th latency telemetry for tenant, rollback plan.
Liam: Can we ship a config snippet customers can paste? e.g.:
```
route_rules:
  - tenant: "acmeplus"
    prefer_model: "redwood-turbo-v2"
    fallback_sequence: ["redwood-lite-quant","redwood-tiny"]
    slo:
      p95_ms: 120
      bucket: short
```

Sophia: We should add automated regression checks in Optimize: when a tenant's fallback rate > 5% trigger alert + suggested tuning.
Maya: Sales asks for estimated delta vs current roadmap. Derek/Liam — ballpark additional ops cost and perf impact?
Derek: Perf: fallback path will increase variance but reduces outages. Ops cost: extra metrics storage (~5-8% at peak), routing metadata ~2%. Dev effort above.
Liam: Model routing will complicate model pin/rollout plans. Need canary per-tenant flow and explicit model-compat checks.
Maya: For ACMEplus we can offer a short-term contract: ship MVP routing + dashboard in 6w, then follow up enforcement + admission control as paid add-on in next quarter.
Sophia: Agree — reduces risk and buys time to build robust enforcement. We should get explicit acceptance criteria: sample traffic replay, SLO dashboard in their account, and a runbook for fallback behavior.
Maya: Action items: 1) Liam/Derek pair to spec the routing API + config by EOD Wed. 2) Sophia to draft Console dashboard mockups by Friday. 3) Sales to confirm ACMEplus OK with staged plan. 4) Add Optimize alert rule stub (Sophia).
Liam: I'll push a minimal API sketch to the product PR: "/v1/routing/policies" with tenant scope and validation.
Derek: I'll prototype fallback pipeline and a perf test harness.
ReleaseBot: deploy scheduled: staging routing feature branch -> canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC :rocket: 
Maya: Thanks — we'll reconvene after the API sketch. Short, focused MVP to keep ACMEplus engaged while we decide on enforcement surface. :thumbsup:
